Theme

Church life · Time, the calendar & feasts

Advent noun

medieval

Vulg. Jac. 5.8: quoniam adventus Dominī appropinquāvit

Adventus, Adventūs m.

noun, fourth declension

Classically an arrival; the Lord’s coming (adventus Dominī) in the Vulgate, and then the Latin rite’s season of the four Sundays before Christmas. The Byzantine rite has instead the forty-day Nativity Fast (see that record).

Examples

  • Venī, redēmptor gentium, ostende partum Virginis; mīrētur omne saeculum: tālis decet partus Deum

    Come, redeemer of the nations, show the Virgin’s child; let every age marvel: such a birth befits GodAmbr. hymn. Intende 5–8

See also the Nativity Fast, Christmas, Christmas Eve.

SourcesLewis & Short: adventus
